transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Thank you for coming in today. What brings you to the clinic? What's been concerning you?

Hi, doctor. Well, I'm here because I've been having a lot of trouble with my eating. 

What really scares me is that once I start eating—especially when I’m alone in the kitchen—it just... it feels like I’ve stepped aside. I can’t make myself stop. Even though I’m telling myself the whole time, "Janet, put it away," I just can't stop doing it. It's gotten to the point where I knew I needed to talk to someone.

After these episodes where you can't stop eating, do you do anything to try to undo it or prevent weight gain—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting food afterward?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything. And I definitely don't exercise a lot. I mostly just... well, I just feel really awful about myself afterward. But no, I don't do anything to try to undo it.
How often would you say these episodes happen—like, how many times per week or per month do you find yourself unable to stop eating like that?

Well, looking back at my kitchen calendar and... thinking about how often I go to the food bank, it's been happening most weeks. I'd say usually once or twice a week. And it's been going on like this for many months now.
During these episodes or afterward, how much do they affect your daily life—like your mood, your work, school, or relationships? Do you find yourself thinking about food or these episodes a lot?

Well, it definitely affects my mood. I spend a lot of time feeling guilty or just... down about it. As for my daily life, I mean, I still show up for my volunteer shifts, and I still go to the craft fairs I help out at. But... I have started avoiding some things. Like, usually after the volunteer shifts, a group of us will go grab a bite to eat. I've been skipping those shared meals lately. I just feel so embarrassed about my eating, and honestly, I don't want people asking me why I seem upset or quiet. So it's easier just to go home.
Has your weight changed over the past year or so? If so, have you noticed it going up, and by roughly how much?
Honestly, I'm not really sure. I... I don't really weigh myself, so I haven't been keeping track of any numbers. I couldn't tell you if my weight has changed or by how much.

During these episodes when you're eating and can't stop, do you feel like you've lost control over how much you're eating, or does it feel like you could stop if you really wanted to but just choose not to?

Well, I definitely feel like I've lost control. What really scares me is that once I start eating... especially when I'm just alone in the kitchen... it feels like I've just stepped aside. I can't make myself stop, even though the whole time I'm telling myself, 'Janet, put it away.' But I just can't.

During these episodes when you can't stop eating, would you say you're consuming a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar situation, or does it feel more like a normal amount of food but you just can't control yourself from eating it?

Yes, it's definitely a much larger amount than what most people would eat. Like, sometimes after I get back from a shift at the food bank, or if I've been baking for an event at the senior center, I'll come home and just... keep going. I'll eat a full plate of leftovers, and then I'll have a few slices of banana bread, some chips, cheese, and whatever cookies are left in the tin. When I finally stop and look at what I've had, I realize it's way more food than I would ever serve to someone else for a meal.

When you're having one of these episodes and eating all that food, would you say the amount you're consuming is objectively larger than what most people would eat, or does it just feel enormous to you even though it might be a normal portion?

I think I just answered that... but yes, it's definitely objectively larger. Like I said, I'll eat a full plate of leftovers, a few slices of bread, chips, cheese, cookies... all in one sitting. It's not just a normal portion that feels big to me. It's a lot of food. Way more than most people would eat at one time.

When you're about to start eating or during these episodes where you can't stop, do you notice any particular emotions or feelings—like stress, anxiety, sadness, or anger—that seem to come up right before or during the binge eating?

I haven't really noticed any specific feelings like that. I don't think I'm particularly stressed or angry right before it happens. It's just... I'm alone in the kitchen, and it starts. I can't really point to a specific emotion that triggers it.
You mentioned feeling guilty and down after these episodes. Would you say that the binge eating and how you feel about yourself because of it causes you significant distress or emotional pain?

I'm not really sure if I would call it significant distress or emotional pain. I mean, I definitely feel guilty and disappointed in myself after it happens, like I said. It bothers me, for sure, but... I don't really know if it's as extreme as emotional pain. I just feel bad about it and wish I hadn't done it.
When you have these eating episodes, does it all happen pretty quickly—like within 30 minutes or so—or does it stretch out over a longer time, like an hour or more?

I'm not exactly sure how long it takes. I haven't really timed it or paid that much attention to the clock when it's happening. It might be 30 minutes, or it could be longer... I just know I eat a lot while I'm standing there, but I couldn't tell you the exact timeframe.

Outside of these episodes where you eat a lot in the kitchen, do you find yourself snacking or eating throughout the day in ways that feel out of control, or is it mainly just during these specific times when you're alone and it all happens at once?

I don't really know if I'd say I snack out of control during the day. I mean, I eat normal meals and maybe a snack here or there, but it doesn't feel like those times in the kitchen. It's mostly just... when I'm by myself in the evening, that's when it all kind of happens at once. The rest of the day feels pretty normal, I guess.
